title: Tool Error Evaluator for Failed Tool Executions
dataSources: Tool Error results on sampled traces in the Agent Stream, read from the logged tool spans
description: Flags traces where a tool the agent called failed to execute, using the Tool Error evaluator in Splunk Agent Observability. This is a different check from choosing the wrong tool.
value: A crashing tool makes the agent apologise, guess or retry, which users see as a bad answer. Separating tool crashes from wrong choices sends the problem to the tool's owner instead of the prompt owner.
implementation: Log every tool call as a tool span with its output, then turn on Tool Error for the Agent Stream with an explicit sample rate. Route flagged tools to their owners. An evaluator scores traces that are already stored and never blocks the reply. To stop or redirect a step inline, use Agent Control (UC-13.8.26).
visualization: Tool Error column in the trace table, grouped by tool span name.
knownFalsePositives: A tool that correctly reports "not found" is not a crash. Check the tool output in the span before filing a bug.
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites

A Splunk Agent Observability project for the application and one Agent Stream per environment or agent inside it. Do not create a second project for the same application: a second project splits the traces. The agent reads `SPLUNK_AO_PROJECT` and `SPLUNK_AO_AGENT_STREAM` from the environment. SaaS tenants authenticate with `SPLUNK_AO_REALM` and `SPLUNK_AO_O11Y_TOKEN`; on-prem tenants with `SPLUNK_AO_API_KEY` plus `SPLUNK_AO_CONSOLE_URL`. Install the SDK with `pip install splunk-ao` (`pip install "splunk-ao[langchain]"` for the LangChain callback).

Step 1 — Instrument the agent

The agent is already instrumented as described in UC-13.8.1: every request is a trace with at least one agent span, LLM spans carry `model`, token counts and the `tools` schemas, and tool spans carry `name`, `duration_ns` and `tool_call_id`.

Step 2 — Configure in Splunk Agent Observability

Evaluators are defined for the organization and turned on per Agent Stream, in the console (Configure Evaluators) or with `enable_evaluators`. That SDK call replaces the stream's set: anything left out is turned off. Evaluators run after the trace is stored, on a sample. A 10% rate stores every trace and scores one in ten, and a sampled trace is scored by every enabled evaluator. There is no documented default sample rate, so set it explicitly.

Step 3 — Validate

Make a test tool raise once against a test stream at a 100% sample rate and confirm the trace is flagged. This use case was written from the Splunk Agent Observability documentation without access to a tenant, so it ships as a draft. Confirm each step in the Splunk Agent Observability console before promoting it.

Step 4 — Operationalize

Review flagged traces by tool span name each week and open bugs against the tool owners.

Step 5 — Troubleshooting

No results: the evaluator is not in the stream's set (`enable_evaluators` replaces the set; see UC-13.8.22), or the trace was not sampled.
grandmaExplanation: We note every time one of the assistant's tools breaks while it is being used, so the right person can fix that tool.

productArtifacts.title: Tool Error evaluator
productArtifacts.body:
Where: Agent Stream > Configure Evaluators (or enable_evaluators in the SDK)
Evaluator: Tool Error
Judge: As listed in the org evaluator catalog
Scores: tool executions in sampled traces
Sample rate: set explicitly for the stream; there is no documented default
Notes: Means the tool execution failed. Wrong tool choice is Tool Selection Quality (UC-13.8.13).
